overview:
FRAME. One merged build plan you can approve in one sitting. This pass applies all 19 of the second critic's fixes on top of pass 1's 17. None is rejected; three are applied in a modified form, with the evidence below. Pass 1's work is all kept:
- jev graph runs and the graph tab
- the network-free mesh view
- sources for the loaded and diff tabs, and precise sentences for the rest
- the installer notice

The 2026-10-07 features are slices:
- web terminals: the perch hosts the PTY and keeps an alacritty screen copy. One SSE carries every terminal. The term plugin uses a scoped token plus chat attribution. The page gets the ⌨ stack and terminal panes.
- the Notepad, with Aoide mail cards and hand-off
- opt-in agent mail send, plus guard rows
- allow for the rest of this chat
- adding update keys from the page

Ground rules:
- eidolon is never edited and EIDO is never decoded.
- Aoide is reached only as a subprocess with --json.
- Two small plugins are new and Minerva-owned: plugins/term and plugins/mail.
- Model spend is $0.

PRIMITIVES AND HOW THEY RELATE
- perch (Rust, one loopback process). It owns doors, runs, terminals, notes, mail cards and allow rules. Every /hub route sits behind the same 6 gates (serve.rs:298-383).
- page (webui/term: Preact + signals + htm, vendored ESM, no build step). It only draws and posts; the truth lives in the perch. Every periodic GET goes through one request lane (core/lane.js), so polls never hold more than one of the browser's 6 connections per host.
- door (eidolon web, one per chat). Its agent reaches the perch only through plugin tools carrying a scoped token. The perch ties each call to a chat by the TCP socket it arrived on: socket -> /proc/net/tcp inode -> door pid -> chat id.
- aoide runner (perch/src/aoide). The one place that builds aoide argv. It always uses an explicit binary path, never a PATH lookup (PATH finds the stale 0.0.25 first).
- guard file (G1). minerva-guard.rn is written beside the member's own policy, so eidolon's permits store stays the one the installer and you write.
- jev and browser services. They are the run's tools. The perch probes /health, and refuses a run unless jev's decision log is off.

CHECKED IN SOURCE (pass 1)
- The mock provider is a fixed script: bash 'ls -1 | head -5', then grep {pattern:'fn main', limit:3}, then text (eidolon/crates/providers/src/catalog.rs:869-886). It can never call term tools.
  - A user tool may register under a built-in's name (rune/src/lib.rs:213-262).
  - Tool scripts get eidolon::tool_call (rune/src/host.rs:699, :1373).
  - So a test-only user tool registered as `grep` in a temp config turns the mock's second scripted call into term_* and mail_send calls made from inside a real door. That proves agent access at $0, with hello.model == mock.
- jev/server.py writes a training row to decisions.jsonl on every choose (:264-320). J1 adds JEV_DECISIONS_LOG=off. /health reports only that the files exist (:370-393), so J1 also adds ckpt and loaded.
- serve.rs:107 throws the peer address away; S0P-a keeps it.
- watch::open has exactly one caller (serve.rs:775). It runs before registry.insert (serve.rs:704-718), so its sink is keyed by the door (pid, port), not by chat id.
- The watcher drops any line over 4096 bytes and never reconnects (watch.rs:196-198, :256). That is A1a's job.
- Registry has no pid -> chat id lookup (sessions.rs:583-595); S0P-a adds it.
- build.sh and nix/plugins.nix copy only browser, jev and subagent (build.sh:104, nix/plugins.nix:7). T3 adds a second source.

CHECKED IN SOURCE (pass 2)
- Where eidolon keeps permits:
  - The store is policy.permits.rn in the same directory as the policy file in force (rune/src/permits.rs:69, :78-80, `policy_path.with_file_name`).
  - The policy path is [policy] path, else config_dir()/policy.rn. config_dir() is XDG's, not the --config file's dir (cli/src/config.rs:698-704, :802-806).
  - So R1a's per-run config, which names no policy, already shares your store.
  - G1 must write its guard beside the member's policy to keep sharing it.
- mode.rs:12-16: policy_in_force reads the member's [policy] path. G1 keeps it reading the member's config, never the generated one, so nothing wraps itself.
- The browser service takes EIDOLON_BROWSER_CHROME, EIDOLON_BROWSER_TOKEN_FILE and EIDOLON_SERVICE_TOKEN (browser/service/src/main.rs:66, :172, :210). The demo can therefore run with no real HOME.
- aoide 0.0.26 --help:
  - `mail export` is read-only, but it writes Markdown per thread for every mailbox and skips receipts.
  - `--hold` needs <node>/<name>.
  - `--from` is attribution only (default AOIDE_SESSION_ID).
  - `--mesh` is required for a node trusted in more than one mesh.
- app.js:
  - the native `term` command is at :525, the ':term :edit :files' row at :500, whereNow at :1525
  - core/hub.js:25-28 holds the list and trash polls
  - api.js:104's whitelist is a prefix test that `tree?` passes, and the files tab calls `tree?session=…` (api.js:133)
- eidolon-plugins tests/jev/stub_service.py:81 serves /health without decisions_log. P1 adds it.

SCOUT DISAGREEMENTS, SETTLED HERE
- Route name: /hub/term for operator routes and /hub/term/a/<verb> for agents. The page scout had /hub/terms.
- Joining late:
  - If the 512 KiB ring still holds output from byte 0, it is replayed exactly.
  - Otherwise the perch sends a snap built from alacritty: RIS, the modes it holds, the grid with SGR runs, and the cursor.
- Input: a raw application/octet-stream body, not base64 JSON.
- term_read waits on a literal substring, not a regex.
- Mail reads:
  - The perch reads as its own reader, AOIDE_SESSION_ID=minerva-perch, which moves only Minerva's own cursor.
  - A --reread at start covers the crash window.
  - `mail export` is non-advancing but returns Markdown threads across all mailboxes with no receipts, so it is not a fit.
- Non-chat panes: one separate ui.xpanes list plus a registry of pane kinds. The ~30 p.s/p.sid sites stay untouched.

CHANGED FROM PASS 1
- Splits: R2 becomes R2a and R2b; R1 becomes R1a and R1b; W2b becomes W2b-1 and W2b-2; S0P and S0W each become a and b. Vendoring moves to V0.
- Decisions go to 10, kept as D1-D6 and D9-D12. D7 (plugins/ in the monorepo) and D8 (cards land in the notes tab) are now planner calls. Their numbers are kept so earlier notes still match.
- Planner calls, not asked:
  - aoide mailbox `minerva`, reader `minerva-perch`, agent sender `minerva-agent`
  - 'this machine' is a send target
  - terminal hold is a header action
  - the agent token is split into a term token and a mail token
  - plugins/term and plugins/mail live in this monorepo (was D7)
  - received cards land in the notes tab, one click from the focused chat (was D8)

PASS 2 CRITIC, FIX BY FIX (pass1_critique_handling style; none rejected)
- 1 (high) G1 moved the permits store: applied-modified.
  - Not (a), manual-only rows: they would not hold in yolo, your default.
  - Not (b), re-applying the installer's rows into a private dir: that drops the trusts you made by hand, and it drifts.
  - Instead, the guard is written beside the member's policy (~/.config/eidolon/minerva-guard.rn unless your config moves the policy). eidolon's beside() rule then keeps the one shared store, and no trust row is re-applied.
  - enabled=true is forced. If the guard cannot be built, chats start unguarded with a sentence.
  - Tests are added, and D9 and D6 are restated with the cost.
- 2 (high) X1/X2 isolation: applied.
  - Every demo process runs under a temp HOME, and Chromium is found through EIDOLON_BROWSER_CHROME.
  - token_file is rewritten to $DEMO paths, and the service token files live under $DEMO.
  - The demo perch has `--knob doors=off`, plus the hello gate.
  - A hash manifest of ~/.config/eidolon is taken before and after X0-X3.
- 3 (high) HUB_PATH: applied with the critic's regex. The files tab is added to the baseline.
- 4 Ownership and waves: applied.
  - S0P-a stubs every submodule with its dispatch arm.
  - T2 moves to W4.
  - S0W-b adds whereOwners, command overrides, keyRows and frameTaps, so T4b never edits app.js.
- 5 Re-asks of rulings 2 and 6: applied.
  - D5 asks only about term_open/term_close. Reach is any web terminal, as ruled. My one statement against it sits in D5's why and is not recommended.
  - D4 asks only about the step-up guard. Removal is offered, per ruling 6.
- 6 Ruling 1 enforced: applied. R1a refuses a start unless jev's /health says decisions_log off. The health probe moves from R1b to R1a.
- 7 Agents and keys: applied. G1 adds keys rows. The limit is stated in D4 and W7.
- 8 Origin: applied. A1a joins each call's origin by call_id, and a rule answers only its own origin.
- 9 Connection lane: applied (core/lane.js). T4a gets a typing-latency live check.
- 10 Agent terminal use with ⌨ closed: applied. frameTaps plus a 5 s roster poll drive a badge and a toast. D11 item 5 switches the rail for the focused chat.
- 11 ssh probe: applied-modified. The probe dials a closed loopback port with every auth method and ~/.ssh config off, so it never reaches your sshd or keys. X3 may use a throwaway sshd.
- 12 Aoide facts: applied.
  - The export claim is corrected.
  - hold is hidden for this machine and explained.
  - --mesh is added.
- 13 alacritty events: applied in T1a, and the allow-listed reply kinds are tested.
- 14 yolo terminal risk and ctx.stop: applied in T2, A1b, T4a and the honest limits.
- 15 Sink door key: applied in S0P-a.
- 16 Ruling 5 narrowings: applied (listed below). The 200-char grey-out is dropped instead: long commands fold and are still matched exactly.
- 17 --from=minerva-agent: applied (R2a, M3, N2b).
- 18 I1 test isolation: applied (explicit --port and --token-file, both asserted).
- 19 D7 and D8 become planner calls, and `:note` is added: applied.

RULING 5 NARROWINGS, ONE LINE EACH (say no to any)
- A structural ask gets no 'allow every <tool>' rule, because eidolon marked it structural for the call's shape, not its name.
- A rule answers only calls of the origin it was made from, so a rule made on a model call never answers a script's nested call.
- Under D10 (a), a rule also ends on a model switch and a perch restart, because it is bound to the door.

SERIALIZING THE HOT FILES (after the seams, each slice owns one folder)
- Perch:
  - S0P-a alone edits serve.rs, lib.rs, main.rs, sessions.rs (two read-only lookups) and the signature of watch::open.
  - S0P-a also writes every <mod>/mod.rs dispatch, with stub submodules.
  - S0P-b alone edits Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, tests/http.rs and the fakes.
  - Afterwards:
    - watch.rs belongs to A1a, spawn.rs to T1a, mode.rs and config.rs to G1
    - pending.rs to R1a (visibility only), tree.rs to R3 (visibility only)
    - the mod.rs state types to R1a, T1a, M2, A1b and AG
- Page:
  - app.js: S0W-a, then S0W-b, then W6, then nobody (later slices register).
  - core/api.js and core/hub.js: S0W-a. core/state.js: S0W-b (one tap line), then W6 (comment), then A2 (send()).
  - index.html: S0W-a and S0W-b. panes/session.js: S0W-b. renderers/index.js: W1, plus one line from T4b. vendor/: V0 only.
- Mechanics:
  - Every executor works in its own git worktree. For Windows worktrees, run git from the Windows side.
  - One shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/minerva-slices-target.
  - The orchestrator reviews, runs the security reviews and the browser-pane checks one at a time, and merges under your git identity with no Claude co-author line.

Waves are in `waves`.

settled_rulings_applied:
Ruling 1 (graph tab, wiki-hop, no training):
- W2b-1/W2b-2 (jev runs) and W3 (the chat's turn graph) share the one graph tab, drawn as our own SVG (W2c) with dagre vendored through vendor/update.sh (V0).
- W2a/W2b-2 show every listed field per step, from the run's own journal: state, options with p, pick, margin vs floor, park, action and result, path, budgets.
- --run-graphs defaults to wiki-hop. The triage graphs (security/escalation loops) are never startable from the page.
- jev/server.py logs a training row on every choose (:264-320), so J1 adds JEV_DECISIONS_LOG=off.
- Enforced in the product, not only in demo envs. R1a refuses a page start with 409 and the start command unless jev's /health reports decisions_log off. An old /health without the field counts as on. W2b-1 shows the refusal. P1 adds the field to the plugin's stub service, so X0 passes.
- Park answers never feed back (interp.rn:399-456 returns an index only). No training slice exists.

Ruling 2 (terminals), applied as written:
- xterm.js 6.0.0, vendored (V0).
- portable-pty + alacritty_terminal in the perch (S0P-b deps, T1a). The alacritty copy is the only query answerer, through one allow-listed reply path.
- SSE plus POST (T1b/T1c).
- The term plugin with term_list/read/send (T3), on a token scoped to terminals (AG). term_send asks in manual (D6).
- Reach is ANY terminal opened from the web, as ruled (T2). Only term_open/term_close, which the ruled tool list does not name, are asked (D5).
- Agents ssh through Minerva terminals: the tool descriptions say so, and D9's ssh row points bash ssh at the term tools.
- The ⌨ rail tab stacks live, foldable views: most recent output on top, the focused chat's agent terminals first (T4a).
- An agent's terminal use reaches the sidebar even with ⌨ closed (T4a): frameTaps on open chat streams, a 5 s roster poll, a ⌨ badge and a toast. For the focused chat the rail switches to ⌨ (D11 item 5).
- ⇱ pops a terminal into a dwindle pane and leaves '→ in a pane' behind; closing the pane returns it (T4b).

Ruling 3 (notepad):
- Notes are <home>/notes/<name>.md, i.e. ~/Minerva/notes (N1).
- `:note [title]` makes one from anywhere (N2a).
- They are sent over Aoide mail only (M2), never by a transport of our own.
- They land as a card the receiver chooses to send (N2b), in the notes tab (a planner call, formerly D8). No route ever posts a card to a door, and the composer prefill is quoted and unsent.
- Aoide gaps are listed for Dev 5.

Ruling 4 (Aoide send in scope):
- Operator mail send (M2/N2b) and right-click 'hand off to a node…' (N2b, mail-only).
- Agent send through mail_send (M3): mail-only, off by default, per-session opt-in, an hourly cap of 10. Its origin is recorded twice:
  - the letter itself carries --from=minerva-agent, which is what Aoide writes as the sender attribution and what the receiver's card shows
  - Minerva's sent.jsonl carries the chat id, which never leaves the node
- It never uses the conduct channel.
- The mesh VIEW stays network-free (R2b). Pass 1's decision 8 ('read-only, never send') is dropped. hub.md 'Never: send' is amended by D1.

Ruling 5 (allow for the rest of this chat):
- A1a: the watcher reads ask frames for every door, page or no page, and joins each ask to its call's origin by call_id.
- A1b: a pure matcher. Tools match by name; bash matches only by its exact input.command plus the door's cwd; a rule answers only its own origin. The perch answers yes with RULE_NOTE.
- Rules are listed in the loaded tab with [ revoke ] (A2) and cleared on a mode switch. D10 asks only whether they also end with the door.
- The three narrowings are told in one line each in the overview. The 200-char grey-out from pass 2's draft is dropped.
- Own security review on A1a, A1b, A2 and XS.

Ruling 6 (installer in the page):
- The update notice and adding keys from the page are kept (I1, R4, W7). Pass 1's 'scope creep' fix stays rejected.
- The fingerprint is typed back on every add. Only the step-up guard is asked (D4).
- Removal is offered for keys 'added by hand', because the installer contract names `keys remove <id> --confirm <FP>`. It is no longer asked.
- The page never offers update.
- Agents share your uid and can use the keys CLI directly. G1 adds deny rows for that, and D4 and W7 state it.
- Signed rotation arrives with `hoot update`. The page shows each key's source and never applies a rotation itself.

Ruling 7 ('make sure everything is working'):
- Every placeholder gets a real source or a precise sentence: W5 (loaded/diff, incl. the guard status line), W6 (run tab, : line, ctx gauge), W4 (mesh), W3 (turn graph), W7 (home), and T4a/N2a replacing the ⌨/✎ stubs.
- X0 smokes every existing feature end to end, plus the new ones, mock-only.

Ruling 8 (manual/auto/yolo per chat, yolo default):
- No slice changes the default.
- G1's deny rows hold in yolo (eidolon/crates/core/src/yolo.rs:19-31 never overrides a deny). G1 writes its guard beside your policy, so the installer's vouches and grants still hold in yolo, auto and page runs.
- Allow rules are offered only where asks exist (auto, manual).
- In yolo the term and mail tools run without asking (mail_send still needs the per-chat opt-in). The ⌨ tab states this at the top for a yolo chat.

Ruling 9 (UI and code style), written into every slice:
- TUI look with bracketed text actions and no button chrome.
- Preact+signals+htm, vendored ESM, no build step (V0 extends update.sh instead of adding a bundler).
- Later page slices register into S0W-b's registries (tabs, pane kinds, commands, whereOwners, keyRows, frameTaps) instead of editing app.js.
- README per new folder: perch/src/<mod>/, webui/term/{graph,mesh,install,terms,notes,allow,tests,vendor}/, plugins/{term,mail}/.
- Rust hand-formatted at about 140 columns, never rustfmt.

pty.rs:
- spawn: openpty + spawn_command run as a job on the existing Spawner thread (spawn.rs gains a generic job kind), so terminal forks never interleave with door forks
- program: CommandBuilder::new_default_prog() (login shell)
- cwd: the given one, which the caller checked, else HOME
- env: the perch's own plus TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor, LANG=C.UTF-8 when unset, MINERVA_TERM=<id>; never a token
- reader: one std thread per terminal: Term.advance -> ring -> notify; above ~8 MiB/s it sleeps 10 ms per slice
- writer: one thread per terminal with a bounded 64 KiB queue
- exit: spawn_blocking(child.wait)
- close: killpg(sid, SIGHUP) and SIGHUP to tcgetpgrp; drop the master; wait 2 s; sweep /proc/*/stat for session == sid and SIGKILL each; reap
- shutdown(ctx): the same for every terminal concurrently, bounded at 2.5 s
The perch is the only answerer, through one function, reply_kind(event) -> Option<bytes>, that every alacritty event passes:
- Event::PtyWrite (alacritty's own answers: DA, DSR/CPR, DECRQM, keyboard mode, CSI 18t text-area size in chars) goes to the writer.
- ColorRequest (OSC 4/10/11/12) is answered from the default theme's palette, fixed in the perch.
- TextAreaSizeRequest (pixels, CSI 14t) is declined, because the perch knows no pixel size.
- ClipboardLoad and ClipboardStore are always refused.
- Anything else is dropped.
- XTVERSION and DECRQSS go unanswered: alacritty does not answer them and the page swallows them, so an app that asks waits out its own timeout. Documented in the README.
screen.rs:

slices.title: Guard rows in the generated policies (all modes), written beside your policy so permits stay shared, + manual credential pre-grants
slices.what:
Per D9. Where the guard lives, checked in source:
- eidolon keeps its permits store as policy.permits.rn beside whichever policy file is in force (rune/src/permits.rs:69, :78-80; cli/src/config.rs:698-704).
- The installer's trust and grants go to the default store (installer/src/plugins.rs:202-210).
- A guard in <home> would have moved auto, yolo and every run onto an empty store.
So:
- auto and yolo:
  - guard::write writes minerva-guard.rn (0600, atomic, rewritten each start) into the directory of the policy eidolon would probe for the member: the member's own [policy] path's dir, else <member config dir> (~/.config/eidolon).
  - beside() then resolves to the very policy.permits.rn the installer and your own `eidolon plugins trust/grant` write, so vouches and grants keep working in auto, yolo and R1a's run configs (which copy config.toml's [policy] path). No trust row is ever re-applied.
  - It is the one Minerva file the perch writes there, besides I1's token files.
- The file's content:
  - the stock table found by mode.rs's policy_in_force, reading the MEMBER's config, never the generated one, so the guard never wraps itself and manual still wraps the stock table
  - its four entry points renamed, as manual does
  - a classify_program wrapper that adds the deny rows and passes every other verdict through unchanged
- config.rs puts [policy] path = that file and enabled = true into the generated <home>/config.toml.
  - A member's enabled = false would otherwise drop the deny rows. Such a member gets eidolon's gate back in Minerva's auto, stated in the loaded tab.
  - yolo keeps passing --yolo.
- manual: the same rows go into the existing manual wrapper ahead of its 'manual mode:' flags. Its own store (<home>/policy.permits.rn) is unchanged.
- Failure mode: config.toml is written without the guard (today's behavior) when any of these happens:
  - the wrap fails (an entry point not found exactly once after an eidolon update)
  - the directory is not writable (a policy in the nix store)
  - a start-up probe `eidolon --config <home>/config.toml policy -- aoide mail send x` does not answer deny
  Auto and yolo still start, and guard::status() carries the sentence that /hub/meta/policy and the loaded tab show ('guard rows are off: <why>'). Yolo is the default, so a broken guard never makes chats unavailable.
Rows:
- (1) DENY when any argv token's basename is aoide, aoide.exe or aoided, or any -c/-e/--command string matches the word aoide or aoided as a command. Reason: "Minerva: agents send Aoide mail with mail_send (opt-in per chat); the aoide CLI is not for agents here".
- (2) DENY when the program is ssh (after stripping env, nohup, timeout, xargs, nice, stdbuf, command, exec and FOO=bar), or a -c string runs ssh. Reason: "Minerva: ssh through a terminal, term_open then term_send, so the operator watches live". scp and rsync are not touched.
- (3) DENY any of these:
  - `minerva keys` with any verb except list and inspect
  - `minerva web --keys-arm`
  - any argv token whose basename is perch-open.sh, together with --keys-arm
  - hoot or hoot.ps1 with `keys`, directly or through powershell.exe/pwsh -File|-Command

honest_limits: jev's confidence is not its quality. jevlike reads only the first 192 bytes of context and 32 bytes per option, and the page shows exactly that cut. Expect parks. No training, by ruling.
It is unverified that jev-base-v0 was trained on wiki-hop's context format, so its probabilities may be close to flat.

Any errored step makes a run impossible to resume (cli/workflow.rs:531-561). A plugin reinstall or graph change between a park and its answer also refuses (hash check). The page can only say so and offer a new run.
Only jev parks can be answered from the page. Gate questions inside a run are declined, because the workflow door's user is NoUser. Manual mode cannot run graphs.
Page runs are refused until your jev service runs J1's code with JEV_DECISIONS_LOG=off. An old service without the field counts as logging. The gate trusts what /health says; it cannot see the file.

The services are pinned to 127.0.0.1:8090/8091 in the plugin tool files, so there is one jev service, one Chromium and one non-terminal run at a time (parked counts). Anything else driving Chromium between a park and its answer makes the replayed click ref stale.
Workflows have no clock. Under D3 (a), a detached run outlives the perch, and only the 200-step host cap bounds it until a perch adopts it again.

Terminals end with the perch, every restart and update included, and that takes an agent's in-flight ssh with it. Only the last screen is kept (terms.json). Survival would need a holder process, which ruling 2 does not have.
Processes that call setsid themselves escape a terminal's close sweep and outlive it.

Agents can read and type into every terminal opened from the web (ruling 2), so whatever is on screen, secrets included, goes to the model provider. A password typed with term_send is kept in the chat log as tool input.

In yolo (the default), agents type into those terminals without asking. That includes terminals you opened that hold a sudo timestamp or a root shell, and the agent may be steered by remote text it read with term_read. [ take over ] is the stop; the ⌨ tab says so at the top.
The term and mail tokens plus socket attribution are a guard rail, not a boundary. A same-uid process can read the master perch token (hub.md:302).
Attribution accepts only doors this perch started. Subagent children, the TUI, workflow runs and a door's own bash children cannot use term or mail tools.

Two terminal emulators run per terminal. The page swallows query replies, and the perch answers through one allow-list. Colour queries see the default theme's palette, not the page's current one. XTVERSION and DECRQSS go unanswered, so an app that asks waits out its own timeout. Pixel-size queries are declined.
VT323 has no box-drawing glyphs, so terminals use system mono (D11). The xterm 6 DOM renderer's cost with 16 live views is unmeasured.

The browser allows 6 connections per host across all tabs. With 3 chat streams, the terminal stream and the poll lane, one connection is left for typing and answers. A second tab of the same profile still competes for the same 6, with no error.
Ctrl+W closes the browser tab, and a page cannot stop it; the guard only asks. Other reserved chords (ctrl+t/n/tab) never reach a terminal.

Guard rows (D9) are a classifier speed bump. Scripts written to disk, base64 or obfuscation get past them, because eidolon has no sandbox and agents share your uid. The term_send text check is the same kind of bump.

To keep eidolon's permits store shared, the guard is the one Minerva file in your eidolon config dir (minerva-guard.rn beside your policy, rewritten each start). If it cannot be built, written or checked, chats start unguarded with a sentence in the loaded tab. A member who set [policy] enabled = false gets eidolon's gate back in Minerva's auto.
In auto, term_send stays un-vouched and asks (D6 a). A per-chat 'allow every term_send' rule makes it silent by your choice, bypassing eidolon's per-command shell classifier.

Allow rules match an exact command, not an exact effect: ./build.sh, make or cargo test run files the model can edit. Rules match the call's origin (joined by call_id), but a user tool registered under the name `bash` and called by the model has the same name and origin, so it inherits bash rules. The model sees RULE_NOTE.
Mail cannot address a chat; the receiver places the card. Note text sits in aoide's argv while it runs (visible in /proc), hence the 64 KiB send cap. Letters carry no attachments.
Held letters (--hold) leave only when the receiving node polls. A Minerva perch never runs `mail poll`, so hold suits only nodes whose own aoide polls, and it is not offered for this machine.

Aoide's one non-advancing read, `mail export`, writes Markdown per thread across every mailbox and skips receipts. Minerva therefore reads with `mail read` as its own reader (minerva-perch), and the start-up --reread recovers the crash window. There is no push for new mail; the perch stats base.jsonl every 5 s while a page is watching.

'Delivered' needs the receiver's ack to come back. This box's A2A door is loopback-only, and cross-node delivery between club machines is unverified. A self-send rings your aoided, and its petname fallback could nudge a conducted session named `minerva` (a Dev 5 ask).
--from is attribution, not authentication. A card's 'minerva-agent' or 'minerva' sender is what the sending perch claimed. The origin chat stays in the sender's sent.jsonl only.
A hand-off is a note (title, project, cwd, last reply, your line), not a session migration. Aoide has none.
Mesh: no live presence, because nothing probes. 'verified' and cached rosters can be stale. Shape drift is invisible (schemaVersion stayed "0"). The vendored aoide-core is 0.0.23 while 0.0.26 runs.

The update notice and keys cannot be checked live on this box (no ~/.local/opt/minerva); they are verified against fake_minerva only. Page-added keys never expire and survive a release-key revocation. If a script in the page's origin rewrites the fingerprint shown, every guard confirms the attacker's key; only comparing with the maintainer's published fingerprint defends.

Agents run as your uid, so one can run `minerva keys add` or read the perch bearer and arm the page itself. G1's keys rows are only a speed bump for that; the page's arm guards only against script in the page's origin.
There is no honest source for persona or effort, and no PR or +/− without running git, which Minerva never does on a folder.
Turn-graph verdicts attach heuristically until upstream gap 14 adds a call id.

The mock model is a fixed script. Agent access is proven through a test-only user tool that shadows `grep` in a temp config, not by a model choosing term tools. Whether the mock repeats its script on a second send is unknown until X0.
Page tests cover pure modules only (node --test, no DOM). Components are proven by browser-pane live checks.

decisions_needed.question: How should the demo's jev service load (no training either way, decision log off, under a temp HOME with the weights read in place)?
options: (a) jev-base-v0.pt + openjev float32 under a 20 GB memory cap, only if X1 measures peak ≤ 16 GB with ≥ 22 GB available
(b) jev-base-v0.pt + an OPENJEV_DTYPE=bfloat16 knob in Minerva's jev/server.py (about 9 GB, CPU speed unmeasured)
(c) synthetic.pt (the toy default)
(d) skip openjev (every hop's entail errors, so the first park cannot be resumed)

decisions_needed.why: jev-base-v0 is the only checkpoint trained on link choice. Without openjev every hop journals an errored step and eidolon refuses to resume any park. The cap keeps an OOM from taking your perch, door or aoided down.
decisions_needed.gates: X1, X2, J1 (bf16 knob only for b)

decisions_needed.question: What happens to a running jev run when the perch stops or restarts (an update included)? Terminals end with the perch either way, because the kernel hangs up a terminal's session when the perch dies, even on SIGKILL.
options: (a) runs detach: no kill_on_drop, output to files in the run dir, and the restarted perch adopts the pid; terminals end, and their last screen is kept as 'ended when the perch stopped'
(b) runs get SIGTERM on a graceful stop (journaled 'cancelled', cannot be resumed); terminals end the same way
